subject: Novara request: priority response & availability commitment — evaluation and ops asks
messages:
From: Sophie Kim <sophie.kim@novara.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: sub-90ms p95 + 99.95% uptime commitment for Novara production

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Novara is excited about Redwood's latency profile. We have a procurement target to land a vendor who can commit to a priority-response commitment for our realtime inference paths. Specifically: 

- p95 response time <= 90ms for text-generation endpoints (payload distribution attached)
- 99.95% monthly uptime for production API calls routed from our US region
- A fallback plan and SLA credits if we miss SLOs for more than two consecutive days

We're asking whether Redwood can support a contractual exception for these commitments for the first 12 months of our enterprise agreement. We understand this is non-trivial — happy to trade price and committed capacity (we're willing to reserve dedicated capacity) if that helps.

Attached is a short SLO request packet with traffic shape and our expected QPS at launch. Can you loop in the product/engineering/legal folks so we can understand feasibility, operational requirements, and a timeline for sign-off? 

Sophie
Sophie Kim
Head of Platform Engineering, Novara
procurement@novara.com

Attachment: novara_slo_request.pdf

Team — forwarding a customer ask. Novara is a mid-enterprise prospect (deal D-2027-1137) pushing for a tight p95 and an uptime carveout. Sophie included QPS and payload distribution (attached).

High-level asks from me:
- Product (Marcus): feasibility notes, whether we can hit sub-90ms p95 on our hosted runtime for their traffic shape and what model variants make sense. Any changes needed to compilation/kernel selection or KV cache behavior?
- Infra/Engineering (Grace): what dedicated capacity / topology (e.g., reserved GPU pool, regional placement) would be required to ensure 99.95% monthly uptime and sub-90ms p95? Ops runbook requirements?
- Legal (Mina): preliminary thoughts on contractual language and typical carveouts we should avoid.
- Sales (Karthik): pricing levers we should propose if we require a commit (reserved capacity, multi-month ramp, premium support).

They explicitly mentioned willingness to reserve dedicated capacity. I'd like a short internal assessment by EOD Wednesday (48 hours) that we can share as an initial feasibility note. If this is doable, we'll ask Novara for a short pilot / load window before contract language.

Forwarded message below.

Marissa — thanks for escalating. Quick assessment from the sales/AM side to help prioritize: Novara is 1) willing to commit dollars and 2) considering a reserved capacity contract to get a stronger SLO. This makes the ask potentially tractable if engineering/product can design a mapped commitment.

Initial thoughts / asks for product & infra:
- Are they asking host-level p95 (end-to-end including network) or Redwood-side p95 (response from our runtime)? Clarify with customer, but we should scope our commitment to run-time latency under reasonably defined network egress windows.
- Suggested commercial path: "Dedicated capacity + priority routing + elevated support" in exchange for a custom SLO and a 12-month reserved commit. We should quantify committed gpus and expected QPS headroom.
- If product/infra require a staged ramp (pilot week, then 30/60/90 day SLAs) we can structure milestones tied to payments.
- Pricing: simple model — base hosted rates + 20–40% premium for guaranteed floor + fixed monthly fee for reserved capacity. Exact numbers after infra estimates.

Asks for Engineering/Product (Marcus, Grace):
1) Marcus: can the runtime guarantee p95 <= 90ms for the model family they plan to use (they listed a 7B opt-style baseline in the attachment)? If not, which model variants or quantization profiles would help?
2) Grace: what dedicated pool size (GPUs and nodes) would you recommend for initial launch (they expect 80 QPS peak), and what operational readiness (on-call escalation, hot spares, cross-region fallback) is required to achieve 99.95% monthly uptime?

Mina — please flag any absolute redlines for contract language (e.g., not accepting continuous uptime guarantees tied to third-party infra outages).

If product/infra can provide a short assessment tomorrow, I can share a scoped proposal with Novara on Thursday and propose a pilot window.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: sub-90ms p95 + 99.95% uptime commitment for Novara production

Team — quick product + infra feasibility summary (answering Karthik's bullets). Apologies for the slight delay; pulled dev-time for profiling.

1) Scope of commitment
- We should define the commitment as "Redwood runtime p95 for requests handled by the dedicated capacity pool, measured at the egress of our runtime (not including Novara's network)". This keeps the SLO limited to our measurable domain and avoids third-party network redlines.

2) Latency feasibility (p95 <= 90ms)
- For the stated model family (7B opt-like), with FP16 and our optimized kernels, runtime p95 under 90ms is achievable at single-request mode with appropriate batching disabled for priority routes. However: typical trade-offs — disabling batching increases per-token costs and reduces throughput efficiency.
- Recommendation: allocate a dedicated pool of 8 A100-class GPUs with low-latency node placement in the US-west region and configure priority routing + single-request fast-path for their priority API keys. This gives headroom for 80 QPS with modest concurrency (we estimate 70–85% utilization at peak).

3) Availability & operational runbook
- To target 99.95% monthly uptime (approx ~22 minutes downtime allowed/month), we need:
  - Hot-standby capacity in a secondary AZ to handle failovers without cold-start model loads.
  - Automated health checks and circuit-breaker-based fallback to a slightly lower-tier model variant for short degradation windows (e.g., fall back to a quantized 7B variant with higher latency but preserved correctness).
  - A runbook for failover, plus a shadowing window during the first 30 days of production.
- Runbook items: activation checklist, on-call rotation with two-day overlap, escalation contact list, warm-restart procedures, and telemetry dashboards (token-level latency histograms, per-node p95 alerts).

4) Commercial / pricing considerations
- Cost impact: moving to single-request priority routing + dedicated pool will likely increase per-token cost by ~30–60% depending on quantization. Recommend offering: reserved capacity discount + monthly fixed fee to cover hot-standby & SLA administration.

5) Contract language notes for Mina
- Proposed wording: Redwood will guarantee runtime p95 <= 90ms for requests routed to the customer's dedicated capacity pool, measured at Redwood's runtime egress. Redwood's uptime commitment will be 99.95% monthly for requests routed to said pool, subject to exclusions (force majeure, customer's network outages, scheduled maintenance with prior notice).
- We should avoid absolute uptime guarantees that do not allow for planned maintenance windows; include a mutually agreed maintenance calendar and pilot ramp milestones.

6) Pilot recommendation
- 7-day pilot with synthetic load to validate p95 targets, then 30-day monitored pilot in production with a lower financial commitment before signing full 12-month reserved contract.

Attachments: operational runbook template and a ballpark cost estimate (will follow as spreadsheet).

Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
